::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
## TL;DR

Climate models usually feed agricultural ammonia ($\text{NH}_3$) in as a fixed offline inventory, so the land and the atmosphere never talk. We built a bidirectional reactive-nitrogen coupler between $\text{CLM5}$ and $\text{CAM6}$ inside $\text{CESM2}$: dynamic emissions come out at $42.3\text{ Tg N yr}^{-1}$, the ammonium nitrate burden rises $72\%$, and the net forcing is $-0.24\text{ W m}^{-2}$ globally and up to $-1.8\text{ W m}^{-2}$ over Asia. After this module you can explain why that cooling masks regional warming and why cleaning the air would unmask it.
:::

## The loop that offline emissions break

In the real Earth system, agricultural nitrogen runs in a closed loop from soil to air and back:

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    Soil["Agricultural Soil (CLM5)<br/>Synthetic N Fertilizer + Manure"] -->|"Dynamic Volatilization (pH, Moisture, Temp)"| AtmGas["Atmospheric NH3 Gas"]
    AtmGas -->|"Thermodynamic Gas-Aerosol Partitioning (MOSAIC/ISORROPIA)"| NitrateAerosol["Ammonium Nitrate Aerosols (NH4NO3)"]
    
    NitrateAerosol -->|Direct Aerosol Scattering| DirectCooling["Direct Radiative Cooling (-0.08 W/m²)"]
    NitrateAerosol -->|"Cloud Condensation Nuclei (CCN)"| IndirectCooling["Cloud Albedo Indirect Cooling (-0.16 W/m²)"]
    
    DirectCooling & IndirectCooling --> TempDrop["Regional Surface Temperature Dimming (-0.15 to -0.35°C)"]
    
    NitrateAerosol -->|Wet & Dry Atmospheric Deposition| NaturalEcosystems["Remote Natural Forests & Grasslands (N Deposition)"]
    NaturalEcosystems -->|"Carbon Sequestration (N-Stimulated Growth)"| CarbonSink["Enhanced Terrestrial Carbon Sink"]

    class Soil olive
    class AtmGas ochre
    class NitrateAerosol indigo
    class TempDrop plum
    class CarbonSink sage
    classDef indigo fill:#1d4a62,stroke:#c97d62,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#ffffff
    classDef plum fill:#48304a,stroke:#c97d62,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#ffffff
    classDef olive fill:#5b6e34,stroke:#c97d62,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#ffffff
    classDef ochre fill:#d69a2e,stroke:#3b1a18,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#3b1a18
    classDef sage fill:#95a87f,stroke:#3b1a18,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#3b1a18
```

Historically, global models broke this loop: land models calculated soil nitrogen without atmospheric chemistry, while atmospheric models prescribed static, fixed monthly ammonia emission inventories[^1].

## Closing the loop inside CESM2

In our paper in *Biogeosciences*[^2], we built a bidirectional land-atmosphere nitrogen coupling inside **CESM2** in three pieces:

1. **Dynamic Soil Volatilization in CLM5**: Rather than static emissions, soil $\text{NH}_3$ volatilization is calculated at every 30-minute model time step as a function of soil ammonium pool size, instantaneous topsoil $\text{pH}$, soil temperature, and moisture content:
   $$E_{\text{NH}_3} = k_{\text{vol}}(T_{\text{soil}}, \theta_{\text{soil}}) \cdot \left[ \text{NH}_4^+ \right]_{\text{soil}} \cdot f(\text{pH})$$
2. **Thermodynamic Gas-Aerosol Equilibrium in CAM6**: Gas-phase $\text{NH}_3$ is dynamically passed through the CESM coupler into CAM6-chem, where it interacts with sulfate and nitric acid ($\text{HNO}_3$) to form fine **ammonium nitrate ($\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$)** and **ammonium sulfate ($(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4$)** aerosols via the Modal Aerosol Module (MAM4)[^3].
3. **Closed Nitrogen Deposition Return**: Wet and dry deposition fluxes are continuously fed back to natural ecosystems in CLM5, stimulating vegetation carbon uptake.

## What the coupled run changes

Coupling changes the emission budget, then the aerosol burden, then the forcing:

| Component | Uncoupled Baseline | Bidirectional Coupled CESM2 | Climate Impact |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Global Agricultural $\text{NH}_3$ Flux** | $34.2\text{ Tg N yr}^{-1}$ (fixed) | **$42.3\text{ Tg N yr}^{-1}$ (dynamic)** | Captures hot-season spikes |
| **Global $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$ Aerosol Burden** | $0.18\text{ Tg}$ | **$0.31\text{ Tg}$ ($+72\%$)** | Substantial aerosol expansion |
| **Direct Aerosol Radiative Forcing** | $-0.03\text{ W m}^{-2}$ | **$-0.08\text{ W m}^{-2}$** | Direct solar reflection |
| **Indirect Cloud Albedo Forcing** | $-0.07\text{ W m}^{-2}$ | **$-0.16\text{ W m}^{-2}$** | Brighter agricultural clouds |
| **Total Effective Radiative Forcing ($\Delta F_{\text{net}}$)** | $-0.10\text{ W m}^{-2}$ | **$-0.24\text{ W m}^{-2}$** | **Net cooling amplification** |
| **Regional Cooling (East Asia & Indo-Gangetic Plain)** | $-0.05^\circ\text{C}$ | **$-0.15\text{ to }-0.35^\circ\text{C}$** | Masks greenhouse warming |

```{=html}

<figcaption><strong>Figure 1 | Fertilizer aerosol cooling is a regional signal that global means all but erase.</strong> Bars run leftward from zero because both pathways cool. Direct scattering by $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$ particles (blue) contributes $-0.58\ \text{W m}^{-2}$ over East Asia and the Indo-Gangetic Plain, while the cloud-albedo response (magenta) contributes more than twice that, $-1.22\ \text{W m}^{-2}$, because the same particles act as cloud condensation nuclei. Together they reach $-1.80\ \text{W m}^{-2}$ locally &#8212; roughly seven times the global-mean $-0.24\ \text{W m}^{-2}$ &#8212; which is why the coupling masks greenhouse warming exactly where the fertilizer is applied and is invisible in a global average.</figcaption>
</figure>
```

### Explore the two levers

Ammonium nitrate needs both ammonia and nitric acid, so move the fertiliser slider and the $\text{NO}_x$ scenario separately and watch which one limits the aerosol:

::: {.sim-card}
#### 🌐 Coupled Land-Atmosphere Nitrogen-Climate Gauge

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof fertPct = Inputs.range([50, 200], {value: 100, step: 10, label: "Global fertilizer application (%)"})
// Inputs.select silently hangs the whole OJS program when the Map values are
// numbers, so the option values stay strings, exactly as the <select> did.
viewof noxOption = Inputs.select(new Map([
  ["Current High NOx (Abundant HNO3)", "1.0"],
  ["Strict Clean Air NOx Controls (-50%)", "0.5"],
  ["Deep Decarbonization NOx (-80%)", "0.2"]
]), {value: "1.0", label: "Industrial NOx emission scenario"})

noxScale = Number(noxOption)

fertScale = fertPct / 100

nh3Flux = (42.3 * fertScale).toFixed(1)

// Ammonium nitrate needs both NH3 and HNO3, hence the joint 0.75-power scaling.
aeroMass = (0.31 * Math.pow(fertScale * noxScale, 0.75)).toFixed(2)

// Forcing and cooling are scaled off the *rounded* burden, as in the original.
rfNet = (-0.24 * aeroMass / 0.31).toFixed(2)
coolMask = (-0.25 * aeroMass / 0.31).toFixed(2)

note = noxScale < 0.4
  ? "⚡ Deep Industrial NOx Abatement: Slashes atmospheric nitric acid, decoupling agricultural ammonia from nitrate aerosol formation and unmasking regional greenhouse warming."
  : fertScale > 1.4
  ? "🌾 Heavy Agricultural Expansion: Surging ammonia emissions drive intense regional aerosol cooling over agricultural breadbaskets, but at the cost of severe particulate air pollution."
  : "🌍 Balanced Coupling: Land-atmosphere nitrogen interactions produce -0.24 W/m² global cooling while sustaining downwind ecosystem nitrogen deposition."

card = (label, value, colour) => html`<div class="sim-readout">
  <div class="sim-readout-label">${label}</div>
  <div class="sim-readout-value" style="color:${colour}">${value}</div>
</div>`

html`<div class="sim-readouts">
  ${card("NH₃ Volatilization", nh3Flux + " Tg N/yr", "#f59e0b")}
  ${card("NH₄NO₃ Aerosol Burden", aeroMass + " Tg", "#38bdf8")}
  ${card("Global Radiative Forcing", rfNet + " W/m²", "#6366f1")}
  ${card("Regional Cooling Mask", coolMask + " °C", "#10b981")}
</div>`

html`<div style="font-size: 0.9em; background: rgba(56, 189, 248, 0.1); border-left: 4px solid #38bdf8; padding: 10px; border-radius: 4px;">${note}</div>`
```
:::

### Data and code

- **Earth System Model**: The bidirectional nitrogen coupler code is implemented in the **Community Earth System Model (CESM2.1 / CAM6-chem / CLM5)**.
- **Model Archives**: Simulation output files and namelists are archived on the [NCAR Climate Data Gateway](https://www.earthsystemgrid.org).
- **Source Scripts**: Analysis and plotting code are hosted on GitHub: [`kamingfung/CESM2-Coupled-Nitrogen`](https://github.com/kamingfung).

## Key takeaways

- Offline ammonia inventories sever the land-atmosphere nitrogen loop; coupling CLM5 volatilisation to CAM6 chemistry at every 30-minute step restores it.
- Dynamic emissions are larger than the fixed inventory ($42.3$ versus $34.2\text{ Tg N yr}^{-1}$) because they capture hot-season spikes, and the ammonium nitrate burden rises $72\%$.
- The aerosols cool: $-0.24\text{ W m}^{-2}$ globally, but $-1.8\text{ W m}^{-2}$ and $-0.15$ to $-0.35^\circ\text{C}$ over East Asia and the Indo-Gangetic Plain. The signal is regional and a global mean hides it.
- Cutting agricultural $\text{NH}_3$ and industrial $\text{NO}_x$ is needed to protect people from $\text{PM}_{2.5}$, and doing so removes this cooling mask and accelerates near-term regional warming.
- Aerosol abatement therefore has to run alongside cuts in short-lived warmers ($\text{CH}_4$, black carbon, hydrofluorocarbons) to avoid a warming step as the air clears.

## References

[^1]: Lamarque, J.-F. et al. The Atmospheric Chemistry and Climate Model Intercomparison Project (ACCMIP): overview and description of models, simulations and evaluation. *Atmos. Chem. Phys.* **13**, 1793–1832 (2013). https://doi.org/10.5194/acp-13-1793-2013
[^2]: Fung, K. M., Val Martin, M. & Tai, A. P. K. Modeling the interinfluence of fertilizer-induced $\text{NH}_3$ emission, nitrogen deposition, and aerosol radiative effects using modified CESM2. *Biogeosciences* **19**, 1635–1655 (2022). https://doi.org/10.5194/bg-19-1635-2022
[^3]: Liu, X. et al. Description and evaluation of a new four-mode version of the Modal Aerosol Module (MAM4) in the Community Atmosphere Model (CAM5). *Geosci. Model Dev.* **9**, 505–526 (2016). https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-9-505-2016
